(Question)

Al-Suhayli said: Among the benefits of this question is that we ask: why did the first verse come with "ʿalā" (على) and the second with "bi" (بـ)?

The answer: we must ask about the meaning for which the Exalted said, ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye﴾ with the particle ʿalā.

And the Exalted said, ﴿It sails under Our eyes﴾ and ﴿Construct the ark under Our eyes﴾ with the particle bi. What is the difference?

The difference is that the first verse came to make manifest a matter that had been hidden and to reveal what had been concealed. Children at that time were nourished and reared in secret, so when it was willed that Moses, peace be upon him, be made and nourished and raised in a state of safety and openness, not under fear and concealment, the particle ʿalā (على) entered the wording as a signal to the meaning, because it conveys elevation (istiʿlāʾ), and elevation is manifestation and display. It is as if the Exalted were saying: "and that you may be raised ʿalā (in the sight of) safety, not under fear."

The mention of the "eye" (ʿayn) is because it includes the meaning of care (riʿāyah) and protection (kalāʾah).

As for His saying, ﴿It sails under Our eyes﴾ and ﴿Construct the ark under Our eyes﴾, He means only care from Us and protection, and He does not intend to reveal anything or to manifest something after it was concealed. Therefore there was no need in the speech for the meaning of ʿalā, unlike what preceded. This is his statement.

He, may God have mercy on him, did not address the reason for the singular there and the plural here, and it is among the most subtle meanings of the verse.

The difference between them appears from the special distinction with which Moses was singled out in His saying, ﴿And I have chosen you for Myself﴾.

This distinction required the other distinction in His saying, ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye﴾, for this addition is an addition of specification.

As for His saying, ﴿It sails under Our eyes﴾ and ﴿Construct the ark under Our eyes﴾, there is not in it the distinction that is in Moses' being made under the eye of the Exalted and His choosing him for Himself.

What He ascribes to Himself with the plural pronoun may mean His angels, as in His saying, ﴿So when We have recited it, follow its recitation﴾,

and His saying, ﴿We relate to you﴾ and its like. So reflect on it.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah 54, verse 24:

His saying ﴿Shall we follow a single human being from among ourselves?﴾ Since the denial was directed at the fact that the one being followed was a human being, that he was one of them, and that he was a single individual, they rejected him. Their denial did not fall on following as such. The implication of their speech was that if he had been an angel, or someone from outside our own group, we would not have been humiliated by his leadership over us; or if he had been a large company, we would not have refused to follow them, and we would have followed them.

**(Digression: On the Arguments of Those Who Hold That the Family of the Prophet ﷺ Are His Ummah and Followers)**

He said, may Allah have mercy on him:

As for the third view, that the family of the Prophet ﷺ are his ummah and his followers until the Day of Resurrection,

its proponents argued for it on the basis that the family of a greatly honoured leader who is followed are those who follow him in his religion and his affair, whether near or distant.

They said: the derivation of this word indicates it, for it comes from *āla*, *ya'ūlu*, meaning "to return," and the followers return to their leader, because he is their imam and their refuge.

They said: For this reason, His Exalted saying ﴿Except the family of Lot. We saved them at dawn﴾ [al-Qamar: 34] means by it his followers and partisans who believed in him, from among his relatives and others.

And His Exalted saying ﴿Admit the family of Pharaoh into the severest punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 46] means by it his followers.

**(Section)**

*Saḥar* (the time before dawn) is of two kinds.

The first is that it is intended as the dawn of a specific day, whether the day is definite or indefinite. In this usage it is an adverbial of time (*ẓarf*) that is not nunated (*ghayr munawwan*), on condition that the day is an adverbial and not a subject or object. Regarding this there are two opinions:

The first: its definiteness is due to the implied meaning of annexation (*iḍāfa*), for you mean the dawn of that day, so the nunation (*tanwīn*) was dropped from it, just as it was dropped from *ajma'* and *akta'* when they are annexed in meaning.

The second opinion, which is the choice of Sibawayh, is that its definiteness is by an implied *al-* (the definite article), as if, when you mention a day before it and make it an adverbial, and then mention *saḥar*, you mean the dawn *of that day*, so you dispense with the *alif* and *lām* by mentioning the day.

This view is more correct because of the difference between *saḥar* and *ajma'*. *Ajma'* is an emphasizer (*tawkīd*) in the position of *kullihi* and *nafsihi*, so it is annexed in meaning to the pronoun of the thing emphasized, and it dispenses with stating that pronoun by mentioning the emphasized noun, because *ajma'* is never used except as a follower of it, and it is never used as a predicate about anything.

This is not the case with *al-saḥar*, because it is like *al-faras* (the horse) and *al-jamal* (the camel). If you annex it, there is no way to avoid stating the annexed-to noun, and it is definite by *al-*, as Sibawayh said:

"All of this is because the day is an adverbial and not an object." So if you said: *karihtu yawma al-sabt saḥar* ("I disliked Saturday's dawn"), *saḥar* would be a substitute (*badal*), just as you say *akaltu al-shāta ra'sahā* ("I ate the sheep, its head").

If it is said: Why do you not say it is a substitute when what precedes it is also an adverbial, since it is part of the day, so it would be a substitution of part for whole, as is the case when the day is an object?

The answer: The difference between them is that a substitute is relied upon, and the substituted-for noun is treated as discarded, and the verb becomes restricted to the substitute after having been general over the substituted-for noun.

So when you say *akaltu al-samakata ra'sahā* ("I ate the fish, its head"), eating applies only to its head, and the rest of it is no longer eaten.

This is not the case with *kharajtu yawma al-jum'a saḥar* ("I went out on Friday at dawn"), because the adverbial is governed by the sense of *fī* ("in"), and *saḥar* is made an adverbial, so the day does not cease to be an adverbial but remains in its state, since it is not a condition of an adverbial that what is placed in it fill it.

So the sentence remains relying upon the day as it was before the mention of *saḥar*.

Yes, and what is broader than the day in meaning, such as the month and the year in which the day is mentioned, and what is broader than the year, such as time in general, each of these is an adverbial for the verb that occurs with *saḥar* by mention. So the mention of *saḥar* does not remove any of them from being an adverbial of the verb. For this reason the sentence relies upon the day and dispenses with it, without renewing the instrument of definiteness, unlike: *karihtu yawma al-sabt saḥaran*.

Or else *al-saḥar* from it must have the substitution.

The difference has thus become clear, and the reason for the dropping of nunation has become clear, because it does not combine with *al-* nor with its meaning. And although it is treated as annexed, as some have claimed, this is also why its nunation is prohibited.

As for what prevents its inflection and its full declension, when you intend it for a day which is an adverbial, if it were fully declinable it would fall outside being of that day, because the adverbial relationship was a link between them and indicated that the dawn is of that day. So if you said: *sīra bi-Zaydin yawma al-jum'a saḥar* ("Zayd was journeyed with on Friday at dawn"),

and you made it an object by extension, it would not be permissible, because there is no link between it and the day.

If you intend this meaning, say: *sīra bi-Zaydin yawma al-jum'a saḥar*, or *al-saḥar minhu*,

so that it is linked to it, because you cannot supply the *alif* and *lām* without pronouncing them, except when the sentence contains something that dispenses with them.

As for when it is a fully declinable noun like the rest of the nouns, it must be defined by what nouns are defined by, or else you make it indefinite, and then it would not be of that day.

If you say: "They have permitted *sīra bi-Zaydin yawmu al-jum'a saḥar*" with *yawmu* in the nominative and *saḥar* in the accusative, then why is it not also permissible to say *yawma al-jum'a saḥaru* with *yawma* in the accusative and *saḥaru* in the nominative?

The answer: Although the day is used broadly, it is an adverbial in meaning, and it encompasses the dawn, while the dawn does not encompass it.

Therefore it is not permissible for *saḥar* to become definite by a semantic definiteness unless it is an adverbial like the day of which it is part, so that placing the day first, while being an adverbial, serves in place of the instrument of definiteness.

[Chapter: The Repelling of Decree by Decree]

Repelling decree by decree (dafʿ al-qadar bi-l-qadar) has two kinds.

The first: repelling a decree whose causes have been established but which has not yet occurred, by means of other causes from the decree that oppose it, so that its occurrence is prevented. Such is repelling an enemy by fighting him, and repelling heat and cold and the like.

The second: repelling a decree that has already occurred and become settled, by another decree that lifts and removes it. Such is repelling the decree of sickness by the decree of treatment, repelling the decree of sin by the decree of repentance, and repelling the decree of evil conduct by the decree of good conduct.

This is the way of those who have knowledge (ʿārifīn) and the way of decrees, not surrendering to them, abandoning movement and resourcefulness. For that is incapacity, and God, exalted is He, blames incapacity. When the servant is overcome, his strategies are exhausted, and no room remains for him, then surrender to the decree and prostration like a corpse before the washer who turns it however he wills is the right course. Here, annihilation in the decree (al-fanāʾ fī l-qadar) is beneficial, in knowledge, state and witnessing.

As for the time of capability and the availability of causes, the beneficial annihilation is that one annihilates from creation by the judgment of God, from his own desire by the command of God, from his will and love by the will and love of God, and from his power and strength by the power, strength and aid of God. This is what realizes the true meaning of "﴿You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help﴾," in knowledge and state. And in God is the seeking of help.

(Section: on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have created everything according to a measure﴾)

Sufyan related from Ziyad ibn Isma'il al-Makhzumi, who said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbbad ibn Jaʿfar told us, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) disputing about the decree, and this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness. The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces, (it will be said), "Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with measure."﴾

Narrated by Muslim. Al-Daraqutni also related from the hadith of Habib ibn ʿAmr al-Ansari, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:

"When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: Where are the adversaries of God? They are the Qadariyyah."

However, al-Daraqutni said of this Habib: "Majhul" (unknown), and the hadith is irregular in its chain and is not established.

Those who dispute about the decree are of two kinds:

The first: one who nullifies God's command and prohibition by His decree and measure, like those who said: ﴿If God had willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers.﴾

The second: one who denies His decree and prior measure.

Both groups are adversaries of God. ʿAwf said: Whoever denies the decree has denied Islam.

Indeed God, blessed and exalted, decreed decrees, created creation by measure, apportioned lifespans by measure, apportioned provisions by measure, apportioned affliction by measure, apportioned well-being by measure, and commanded and prohibited.

Imam Ahmad said: "The qadar is the power of God."

Ibn ʿAqil greatly approved of this statement and said: "This indicates the precision of Ahmad's knowledge and his depth in knowing the foundations of religion."

And it is as Abu l-Wafaʾ said: Denying the decree is denying the Lord's power to create the deeds of His servants, to record them and to measure them. The early Qadariyyah denied His knowledge of them, and they are the ones on whose disbelief the early community (salaf al-ummah) agreed. We will mention this later, God willing.

In the Tafsir of ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear God﴾

He said: "Those who say that God is capable of everything."

This is from Ibn ʿAbbas's understanding and knowledge of interpretation and his grasp of the realities of the Names and Attributes, for most of the people of kalam do not give this sentence its due. Even if they affirm it, the deniers of the decree and of the creation of the acts of servants do not affirm it as it truly is. The deniers of the Lord's acts that subsist in Him do not affirm it as it truly is, but rather they openly declare that He is not capable of an act that subsists in Him.

Whoever does not affirm that God is, ﴿every day in a matter﴾, doing what He wills, does not affirm that God is capable of everything. Whoever does not affirm that the hearts of the servants are between two fingers of the Merciful, He turns them as He wills, that He, glorified is He, truly is the Turner of hearts, and that if He wills to make the heart firm He makes it firm, and if He wills to make it swerve He makes it swerve, does not affirm that God is capable of everything. Whoever does not affirm that He established Himself upon His Throne after creating the heavens and the earth, that He descends every night to the lowest heaven and says, "Who will ask Me, that I may give to him? Who will seek My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?", that He spoke to Moses from the tree, that He descends to the earth before the Day of Resurrection when it is empty of its inhabitants, that He comes on the Day of Resurrection to judge between His servants, that He manifests Himself to them laughing, that He shows them His holy self, that He places His foot upon the Fire so that its people are constricted and it draws in upon itself... and other of His affairs and acts, whoever does not affirm these does not affirm that He is capable of everything.

Ah, what a word from the scholar of this community and the interpreter of the Qur'an!

Ibn ʿAbbas was severe toward the Qadariyyah, and so were the Companions, may God be pleased with them.

(Section)

Al-Bukhari said: And Amr ibn Muhammad told us, who said: Ibn ʿUyaynah told us, from Amr, from Tawus, from Ibn ʿUmar:

"Everything is by measure, even your placing your hand upon your cheek."

Al-Bukhari said: Isma'il told me, who said: Malik told me, from Ziyad ibn Saʿd, from ʿAmr ibn Muslim, from Tawus, who said: "I met people of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) who used to say: Everything is by measure, even incapacity and shrewdness."

Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from Tawus.

He said: I heard ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:

"Everything is by measure, even incapacity and shrewdness."

Al-Bukhari said: Layth related from Tawus, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "﴿Indeed, all things We have created with measure﴾ — even incapacity and shrewdness."

Al-Bukhari said: I heard ʿUbaydullah ibn Saʿid say: I heard Yahya ibn Saʿid say: "I have always heard our companions say: The acts of servants are created." Al-Bukhari said: "Their movements, their voices, their earnings and their writing are created."

Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to teach us the istikharah in matters just as he taught us a surah of the Qur'an. He would say: When one of you is concerned about a matter, let him pray two rak'ahs other than the obligatory prayer, then let him say: O God, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge, and I seek power by Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty, for You have power and I have no power, You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen. O God, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood and the outcome of my affair, then decree it for me, make it easy for me, then bless me in it. And if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood and the outcome of my affair, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, and decree for me the good wherever it may be, then make me content with it." He said: "and he names his need."

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih hadith.

So his saying "When one of you is concerned about a matter" is explicit that it is a voluntary act connected to the servant's will.

Knowing this, his saying "I seek power by Your power" means: I ask You to empower me to do it by Your power. It is known that he did not ask for the enabling capacity which is soundness of the limbs and health of the body, but rather he asked for the capacity that brings about the act. So it is understood that it is power decreed by God and created by Him. He confirmed this with his saying: "for You have power and I have no power," that is: You have the power to make me capable and active, and I have no power to make myself so.

Likewise his saying: "You know and I do not know," that is, the true knowledge of the outcomes of affairs, their end, what is beneficial and harmful in them, is with You and not with me.

His saying "make it easy for me" or "turn it away from me" is a request from God to facilitate it if there is a benefit in it for him, and to turn him away from it if there is harm in it.

This facilitation and turning away includes casting the motive for the act into the heart, or casting the motive for abandonment into it. When the motive to act arises, the act occurs, and when the motive to abandon arises, the act is prevented.

According to the Qadariyyah, the preponderance of the servant's agency over abandonment belongs to him alone, the Lord has no hand or influence in it, so asking for this facilitation has no meaning for them, for the facilitation of causes over which the servant has no power exists, and the servant did not ask for it.

His saying "then make me content with it" indicates that the attainment of contentment, which is a voluntary act of the hearts, is a matter that is possible and subject to the Lord, exalted is He, who makes him content.

His saying "turn it away from me and turn me away from it" is explicit that He, glorified is He, is the one who turns His servant away from his voluntary act when He wills to turn him from it, as He said, exalted is He, concerning Joseph the Righteous: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil and immorality.﴾ Turning away evil and immorality is turning away the motives of the heart and its inclination toward them, so they turn away from him when their motives are turned away.

His saying "and decree for me the good wherever it may be" encompasses the good that is within the servant's capacity, his obedience, and the good that is not within his capacity. So it is known that the servant's performance of obedience and good is a matter decreed by God; if God does not decree it for His servant, it does not occur from the servant.

In this hadith is the cure for the question of the decree.

The Prophet (ﷺ) instructed the one who makes this supplication to precede this prayer with two rak'ahs as an act of servitude before his private supplication, and that they be other than the obligatory prayer, so that their performance is purely for this sought purpose.

Since the voluntary act depends on knowledge, power and will, and is not realized except by them, the supplicant seeks God by His knowledge, His power and His will, which He grants by His bounty. He affirmed this meaning by stripping himself of these and disclaiming them, saying: "You know and I do not know, and You have power and I have no power."

He instructed the supplicant to make facilitation conditional upon the good and turning away conditional upon the evil, which is God's knowledge, as a realization of entrusting the matter to Him and a confession of the servant's ignorance of the outcomes of affairs, just as he confessed his incapacity. In this supplication is the giving of servanthood its due and the giving of lordship its due. And in God is the seeking of help.

(Section)

He said in (Tariq al-Hijratayn):

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have created everything according to a measure﴾ [al-Qamar: 49]:

God created all creation by measure, and He created good and evil. The best of good is happiness, and the worst of evil is wretchedness.

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu l-Aswad al-Du'ali, who said: ʿImran ibn Husayn said to me: "Do you see what people do today and strive for? Is it a thing decreed upon them and past from a measure that preceded, or is it about what they will face from what their Prophet brought them and by which the proof was established?" I said: "No, rather it is about what was decreed upon them and passed." He said: "Would that be injustice?" I was greatly alarmed and said: "Nothing exists except that He created it and owns it: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.﴾" He said: "May God guide you aright. I only asked you to test your intellect. A man from Muzaynah, or Juhaynah, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of God, do you see what people do and strive in? Is it a thing decreed upon them and passed, or is it about what they will face from what their Prophet brought them?' He said: 'It is about what was decreed upon them and passed.' The man said: 'Then what is the point of action?' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever God created for one of the two abodes, He will make him work for it.' And the confirmation of this is in the Book of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿And a soul and He who proportioned it, and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness.﴾"

Mujahid, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I know what you do not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30], said: "He knew Iblis's disobedience and created it for him."

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿A group He guided, and a group upon whom error was due﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 30].

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "God, glorified is He, began the creation of the children of Adam as believers and disbelievers, then said: ﴿He it is who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you a believer﴾ [al-Taghabun: 2], and then He will return them on the Day of Resurrection as He began their creation: believer and disbeliever."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And know that God intervenes between a man and his heart﴾ [al-Anfal: 24], said: "He intervenes between the believer and disbelief and the disobedience of God, and He intervenes between the disbeliever and faith and the obedience of God."

Ibn ʿAbbas, Malik and a group of the early scholars said regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy, and for that He created them﴾ [Hud: 118-119]. They said: "He created the people of mercy for mercy, and the people of difference for difference."

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if God had willed, they would not have fought one another﴾ [al-Baqarah: 253]; ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13]; ﴿And if your Lord had willed, all of those on earth would have believed, all of them together﴾ [Yunus: 99]; ﴿And if God had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 35]; ﴿And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it﴾ [al-An'am: 112].

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God or denies His signs? Those will receive their share from the Book﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 37], i.e., their share of what was written for them. And He said: ﴿Thus We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the criminals﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 200]. Al-Hasan and others said: "Shirk and denial."

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 7]. Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi said: "God, glorified is He, inscribed the record of the wicked at the bottom of the earth, so they work by what was decreed to be inscribed for them in that record, and the record of the righteous He placed in ʿIlliyyin, so they are brought to do what was decreed to be inscribed for them in that record."

Ibn ʿAbbas said regarding ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ [al-Masad: 1]: "By what flowed from the Pen onto the Preserved Tablet."

Mujahid, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier﴾ [Ya-Sin: 9], said: "From the truth."

And regarding His saying: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾ [al-Isra': 46], he said: "The quiver contains the arrows." Ibn ʿAbbas said regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And God misled him knowingly﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23]: "He misled him in His prior knowledge." He said, regarding His saying recounting His enemy Iblis: ﴿Because You have sent me astray﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 16]: "You misled me." He said regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, you cannot lead astray [anyone] except those destined for the Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 162-163]: "Those for whom You have decreed that they will burn in Hell."

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said: "If God had willed that He not be disobeyed, He would not have created Iblis." And "He has explained and made clear to you what you are upon, and you cannot lead astray except those decreed to burn in Hell."

Wuhayb ibn Khalid said: Khalid told us: I said to al-Hasan: "Was Adam created for this heaven, or for the earth?" He said: "No, rather for the earth." I said: "Do you see if he had refrained from the sin and not committed it, would he have been left in Paradise?" He said: "Glory be to God! Was there any alternative for him but to commit it?"

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command﴾ [al-Anbiya': 73]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We made them leaders calling to the Fire﴾ [al-Qasas: 41], and He said: ﴿And make us leaders for the righteous﴾ [al-Furqan: 74], i.e., leaders by whom one is guided, and do not make us misguided leaders calling to the Fire. And He said: ﴿And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. And He said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am: 110]. And He said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We gathered against them all things before them, they would not have believed unless God willed﴾ [al-An'am: 111].

Zayd ibn Aslam said: "By God, the Qadariyyah did not say as God said, nor as His messengers said, nor as the people of Paradise said, nor as the people of the Fire said, nor as their brother Iblis said. God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And you do not will except that God wills﴾ [al-Takwir: 29]. The angels said: ﴿We have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾ [al-Baqarah: 32]. Shu'ayb said: ﴿It is not for us to return to it except that God wills﴾ [al-A'raf: 89]. The people of Paradise said: ﴿Praise be to God, who guided us to this. We would not have been guided had God not guided us﴾ [al-A'raf: 43]. The people of the Fire said: ﴿Our misery overcame us﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 106]. Their brother Iblis said: ﴿My Lord, because You have sent me astray﴾ [al-Hijr: 39]."

Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird to his neck﴾ [al-Isra': 13], said: "It is written on his neck: wretched or happy."

Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding His words, ﴿And whoever Allah intends for his trial, you cannot avail him anything from Allah﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 41]: "He means: whoever Allah intends for his misguidance, [your efforts] will not avail him anything."

al-Tabari and others related, through the chain of Suwayd ibn Sa'd, from Sawwar ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Hamzah, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas: The Prophet (ﷺ) ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then extended his right hand and said: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A book from Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, for the people of Paradise, by their names, the names of their fathers, their tribes and their clans. Their first is joined to their last, and nothing will be decreased from them or added to them. Your Lord has finished [the decree]. Yet a person of felicity may be made to follow the path of wretchedness, until it is said of him: he is indistinguishable from them, indeed he is one of them. Then what had preceded for him from Allah of felicity turns him back, and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it before his death by the interval of a she-camel's milking. And a person of wretchedness may be made to follow the path of felicity, until it is said of him: he is indistinguishable from them, indeed he is one of them. Then what had preceded for him from Allah turns him back, and he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it, even if only before his death by the interval of a she-camel's milking. So the one who is destined for Paradise is sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise, even if he does the deeds of the people of the Fire; and the one destined for the Fire is sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire, even if he does the deeds of the people of Paradise." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Actions are by their final outcomes."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is alike for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 6],

and regarding His words, ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have brought them together upon guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 35], and regarding His words, ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam, and whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted﴾ [al-An'am: 125],

and regarding His words, ﴿They would not have believed unless Allah willed﴾ [al-An'am: 111],

and regarding His words, ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13],

and His words, ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on the earth would have believed, all of them together﴾ [Yunus: 99], and His words, ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks﴾ [Ya-Sin: 8],

and His words, ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance﴾ [al-Kahf: 28],

and similar verses of the Qur'an. The Messenger of Allah used to be eager that all people would believe and follow him upon guidance, so Allah informed him that none believes except one for whom felicity had preceded from Allah in the first Remembrance (al-dhikr al-awwal, the eternal decree recorded before creation). Then He said to His Prophet: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 3], and He says: ﴿If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the heaven, and their necks would remain humbled before it﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 4], then He said: ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him﴾ [Fatir: 2], and He says: ﴿You have no part in the affair﴾ [Al 'Imran: 128].

In Sahih Muslim, from Tawus: "I met people from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah who used to say: everything is by qadar (divine decree)." And I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Everything is by qadar, even incapacity and intelligence (al-kays)."

Also in Sahih Muslim, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah wrote the measures of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, while His Throne was upon the water."

Also in his Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not be incapable. If something befalls you, do not say: 'If only I had done such and such.' Rather say: 'Allah decreed, and He does what He wills.' For 'if only' opens the way for the work of Satan."

Also in his Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a vow does not bring to the son of Adam anything that Allah had not already decreed for him. Rather, the vow coincides with qadar, and by it something is extracted from the miser that he would not otherwise have been willing to give."

In the hadith of Jibril and his question to the Prophet (ﷺ) about faith, [the Prophet said]: "Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Decree (al-qadar), its good and its evil."

In the two Sahihs is the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud concerning the creation of the embryo, in which [the Prophet said]: "By Him other than whom there is no god, indeed one of you does the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only a cubit, and then the Decree (al-kitab) precedes him, so he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters the Fire. And indeed one of you does the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is between him and it only a cubit, and then the Decree precedes him, so he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it."

al-Tabari mentioned al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Tusi, who said: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Asfati al-Basri, the muhaddith of Basra, informed us: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a dream, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud has reached me from the truthful one, the believed one (al-sadiq al-masdug), I mean the hadith on qadar." He said: "Yes, by Allah other than whom there is no god, I related it." May Allah have mercy on 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud for relating it, and may Allah have mercy on [the one] who related it, and may Allah have mercy on al-A'mash for relating it, and may Allah have mercy on whoever related it before al-A'mash, and may Allah have mercy on whoever relates it after al-A'mash.

In Sahih Muslim, from Ibn Mas'ud: "The wretched one is he who was made wretched in his mother's womb, and the happy one is he who takes warning from others."

The hadith of the decree of felicity and wretchedness in the mother's womb has been related from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Anas ibn Malik, 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, 'A'ishah the Mother of the Believers, Hudhayfah ibn Usayd, and Abu Hurayrah.

Abu al-Hasan ibn 'Ubayd al-Hafiz said: I heard Abu 'Abdullah ibn Abi Khaythamah say: I heard 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas say: I descended from Samarra to Baghdad on some need of mine. While I was walking along part of the road, I came upon a skull that had rotted, so I picked it up, and on the forehead was written "wretched" (shaqiy), with the letter ya' (ي) pointed downward (kasrah)."

All of these are imams and huffaz (memorizers of hadith). al-Tabari mentioned it in al-Sunnah.

In the two Sahihs is the hadith of 'Ali from the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is none of you but his seat in the Fire and his seat in Paradise have been written." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely upon our writing and abandon action?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy for that for which he was created. As for the one who is of the people of felicity, he is made easy for the deeds of the people of felicity; and as for the one who is of the people of wretchedness, he is made easy for the deeds of the people of wretchedness."

Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah] and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾ [al-Layl: 5-10].

In the two Sahihs, from 'Imran ibn Husayn: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Are the people of Paradise known from the people of the Fire?" He said: "Yes." It was said to him: "Then why do people work?" He said: "Yes, each is made easy for that for which he was created."

In Sahih Muslim, from 'A'ishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was called to the funeral of a boy from the Ansar. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, good tidings for this one, a sparrow from the sparrows of Paradise, who did not reach evil nor commit it.' He said: 'Or otherwise. Indeed Allah, the Exalted, created for Paradise people, He created them for it while they were in their fathers' loins, and He created for the Fire people, He created them for it while they were in their fathers' loins.'"

In the two Sahihs, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The boy whom al-Khidr killed was sealed on the day he was sealed as a disbeliever, and if he had lived he would have burdened his parents with transgression and disbelief."

In Musnad al-Imam Ahmad, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah created the creation in darkness, then cast upon them of His light." In another wording: "So He made them one [entity]. He took of His light and cast it upon that darkness. Whoever is struck by the light is guided, and whoever is missed by it goes astray. Therefore I say: the pen has dried upon the knowledge of Allah."

Rashid ibn Sa'd related from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that Abu Qatadah heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Allah created Adam and brought forth the creation from his back, and said: 'These are for Paradise and I do not mind; and these are for the Fire and I do not mind.'" [Abu Qatadah] said: It was asked: "Upon what do we act?" He said: "Upon the places where the decree falls."

Abu Dawud, in his book al-Qadar, related from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he passed by a man, and [people] said: "This is so-and-so," and they reviled him. 'Abdullah said: "Do you see that if you cut off his hand, could you create for him a hand?" They said: "No." He said: "If you cut off his leg, could you create for him a leg?" They said: "No."

He said: "If you cut off his head, could you create for him a head?" They said: "No." He said: "Just as you cannot change his creation, you cannot change his character. When the drop [of semen] falls into the womb, Allah sends an angel who writes his term, his deeds, his provision, and whether he will be wretched or happy."

In the same book, from Ibn Mas'ud, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ): "There are only two: guidance and speech. The best speech is the speech of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad. The worst of affairs are their novelties, and every innovation is misguidance. Everything that is to come is near. The wretched one is he who was made wretched in his mother's womb, and the happy one is he who takes warning from others."

Ibn Wahb said: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hunaydah related to him that 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah wills to create a soul, the angel of the wombs says, 'O Lord, male or female?' and Allah decrees His command. Then he says, 'O Lord, wretched or happy?' and Allah decrees His command. Then he writes between its eyes what it will encounter, even the stumble that it stumbles upon."

al-Layth related from 'Aqil, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the same, and he mentioned it. al-Zuhri said: and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Udhaynah related to me from Ibn 'Umar the same.

If it is said: What is the difference between the decree being good and evil, and its being sweet and bitter?

It is said: Sweetness and bitterness return to the direct engagement with causes in the immediate, while good and evil return to the goodness and badness of the outcome. So it is sweet and bitter at its beginning and onset, and good and evil at its end and final outcome. Allah, glory be to Him, has established His custom and practice that the sweetness of causes in the immediate is followed by bitterness in the deferred, and their bitterness is followed by sweetness. Thus the sweetness of this world is the bitterness of the Hereafter, and the bitterness of this world is the sweetness of the Hereafter. His wisdom, glory be to Him, has required that pleasures produce pains and pains produce pleasures. Qadar and qada' are arranged in this order with an arrangement from which nothing whatsoever escapes. Evil returns to pleasures and their causes, while the sought-after good is lasting pleasure, and the feared evil is lasting pain. So the causes of these evils, though they include some pleasure, and the causes of those goods, though they include some pain, a pain that is followed by lasting pleasure is more worthy of preference and endurance than a pleasure followed by lasting pain. The pleasure of an hour set against a long pain is not pleasure at all, and the pain of an hour set against a long pleasure is not pain at all.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 54, verse 52:

Ata' and Muqatil said: "Everything they did is written against them in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz)."

Hammad ibn Zayd narrated from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, regarding ﴿And everything they did is in the scriptures﴾.

He said: "It was written against them before they did it."

A group said: "The meaning is that it is counted against them in the books of their deeds."

Abu Ishaq combined the two views, saying: "It is written against them before they do it, and it is written against them when they do it, for recompense."

This is the most correct view. And success is from Allah.

Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 54, verses 54–55:

He named Paradise "a seat of truth" (maq'ad sidq) because every desirable thing is obtained in the good seat there, just as it is said: "a sincere affection" (mawaddah sadiqah) when it is firm and complete, "a sincere sweetness" (halawah sadiqah), and "a sincere sentence" (jumlah sadiqah). From this comes "true speech" (al-kalam al-sidq), because its intended purpose is achieved by it.

The root meaning of this word in their usage is soundness and perfection. From it come truthfulness in speech (al-sidq fi'l-hadith) and truthfulness in deed (al-sidq fi'l-'amal), and the siddiq (the one whose words are confirmed by his deeds). Al-sadaq (with a fatha on the sad) means the hard shaft of spears. It is said of a brave man that he is dhu mus'daq, meaning that his whole constitution is sound. Hadha misdaq hadha means "this is what confirms that," that is, what verifies it. From it comes al-sadaqah (friendship), because of the purity of affection and companionship, and from it come sadaqani al-qital (the battle proved true to me) and sadaqani al-mawaddah (the affection proved true to me).

From it also come qadam sidq (a true standing), lisan sidq (a true tongue), madkhal sidq (a true entrance), and makhraj sidq (a true exit).

All of this applies to the established, intended truth that is desired, in contrast to falsehood (al-kidhb), the vain thing that has no substance beneath it and contains no firm matter.

Some commentators explained "qadam sidq" as Paradise, others as the deeds by which Paradise is attained, others as the precedence that was granted to them from Allah, and others as the Messenger through whose hand and guidance they attained it.

The verified position is that all of these are true, for they were granted from Allah the best reward (al-husna) by that precedence, that is, by the causes He decreed for them through His Messenger, and He stored up their recompense for the Day of meeting Him. "Lisan sidq" is the tongue of true praise for excellent deeds and beautiful ways. In its being a "tongue of truth" there is an indication that it conforms to reality and that it is praise that is deserved, not praise that is false. "Madkhal sidq" and "makhraj sidq" are the entrance and exit in which their possessor is a guarantor upon Allah; it is an entering and exiting by Allah and for Allah.

This supplication is among the most beneficial supplications for a servant, for he is always entering into a matter and exiting from a matter. Whenever his entering is for Allah and by Allah, and his exiting is likewise, he has entered a true entrance and exited a true exit. And Allah is the One sought for help.

((The Eighteenth Part))
